utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I notice that Mr. Milan Simic is not here. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I went this morning to the UNDU facility, and I talked to my client. He's actually very ill. He stayed in bed all day long. And he waived his rights to be present here today. So I really -- he doesn't know, and he's not feeling well as yet, so he doesn't know whether he will be able to come tomorrow or not. That is really beyond me. And I will inform the Trial Chamber as -- tomorrow morning accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: As to what the progress is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. On the document which was discussed yesterday, I would like to find out the position of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. It's my understanding that in relation to this witness, there are two documents which were put on the record as the Defence not having had. One of them was Mr. Pantelic said that they had not received a statement given to the MUP in Bosanski -- Bosanski Samac at the time. That statement was disclosed on the 15th of May, and there are copies of the receipts available, both the original for inspection and copies available if the Chamber or any members of the Defence would like it. With respect to the second document, which were the notes from July 1998, having checked the records, those were not disclosed, and for that oversight, we have to apologise to the Trial Chamber for the inconvenience caused, and of course to our learned colleagues on the Defence for that lack of statement in their file. There was a check done on all witnesses after the pre-trial brief was filed and prior to the Pre-Trial Conference, and during that check a number of documents came up as possibly not having been disclosed. A list was compiled, and they were disclosed on the 15th of May, which is when the other documents were disclosed. For an oversight, I can only put down to human error, [redacted]--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of the witness on the stand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in fact, we are not speaking about formal or informal notes. We are speaking about the statement. That's first fact. Another fact, we have checked our records and we have to inform this Trial Chamber that the statement mentioned that the Prosecution gave with -- of this witness in 1994, we are speaking about statement which was given before the authorities and representatives in, I would say, it's not Orasje, it's Modrica, Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Muslim Herceg-Bosna entity, municipality Modrica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you can give us that name again because you have to identify the authorities correctly for the Prosecution to be able to explain, if they have to explain anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We are speaking about a document with ERN number 0063 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you slow down, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, the document in question is numbered with ERN numbers 00636820. That's the first page. And the second page, accordingly is the last two digits are 21. The document in question is statement of the witness now in bench, and he gave it to -- on a date 27 July, 1994, and he gave this statement to the following -- I will just read the title of the authority, which is the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Ministry of Interior, Derventa Police Administration, Bosanski Samac Police Station. In 1994, that was the organisation, I don't know how in Herceg-Bosna. Again, having checked our records, we can confirm that we have only English version of this statement from 1994. We all know that the obligation during the discovery process of the Prosecution should be that also in B/C/S language, this statement should be provided to our clients, which was not done, and we haven't received any such document. And finally, Your Honours, I kindly invite my friends from the Prosecution to confirm or to inform this Trial Chamber and Defence whether they are in possession of any formal, official statement of all witnesses in this case, given to the Bosnian authorities, Croatian authorities or third parties, and whether these statements are of any relevance to these proceedings. I mean shortly, we all know that in preparation of the case, Prosecutor should rely on certain sources. Basically these sources are -- in our particular case are Muslim intelligence service from Sarajevo called AID, and also some Croatian -- well, authorities, police, and some other secret services. And then Prosecutor is going to bring this case before this -- the other Trial Chamber for the confirmation, et cetera. So it is illogical for us that we have only several previous statements, such as this one from 1994, up to now. Of course, we learned just this afternoon that two statements, including one statement which is related to the next witness, was discovered to the Defence exactly at two hours and 15 minutes p.m., just virtually 20 minutes before. So all of these details raise certain concern on the side of the Defence that the Prosecution is in possession of certain numbers of statements or documents which might be of importance for this case. Of course, in next few months or -- I mean, in a period which is in front of us, the Defence will of course, with the assistance of this Honourable Trial Chamber, try to provide judicial assistance to check everything on side, I mean within the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia and all the other police stations to see whether there was any kind of official connection between -- and communications between these units and the Prosecution. Then we shall be in a situation to inform this Trial Chamber about the details. Thank you very much for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it related to the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is related to the documents. I have a certain submission to make to this point. Your Honours, we understand that this thing can happen, okay? We agree with our learned colleagues from the Prosecutor's side. But the problem here is that Mr. Esad Dagovic is the next witness and his statement has just been disclosed to us. We are -- we want to be very reasonable, and since my client is not present, I will have to have some instructions. I can do it over the telephone but I was thinking to suggest to the Trial Chamber that, after we finish the cross-examination of this witness, that we have a break of -- I mean, within our break of half an hour plus additional 15 to 20 minutes so we can prepare for the cross-examination of Mr. Esad Dagovic in light of this statement that was disclosed to us 20 minutes before. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, one other thing, since this is a protected witness, my learned colleague has somehow missed, and his name is on the record. So it has to be deleted. It's page 2, row 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think the registry did take note of that. Thank you. Yes. Any comments from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll deal with Mr. Zecevic's submission first. Of course, this statement from Mr. Dagovic was correctly only disclosed, and we certainly feel it will be reasonable for them to have more time. It was a single one-page statement involving one incident, and I said it was simply an oversight. With respect to the other matters which Mr. Pantelic has raised before the Chamber, I think any suggestion he's making, and I don't think it's an unreasonable inference to draw from his comments that we somehow are sitting on statements or have -- are deliberately making judgement calls on whether we should be disclosing statements is completely and totally wrong. This case has been a long time in the Tribunal, and it has had a very lengthy pre-trial process, and with that the individual members of the Prosecution team have turned over, but I can say that my colleague -- one colleague -- my predecessor, or our predecessor, was certainly very conscientious of disclosing documents. Errors have happened and it's not foolproof, but there has been no attempt, as has been suggested, to withhold any documents. On the 15th of May, on the signed receipt from Mr. Pantelic, there are a number of statements which were not made to ICTY but were made to local authorities of one nature or another which were disclosed to the -- to the Defence, including the English version of the statement Mr. Pantelic has just talked about. And I have to say I find it somewhat disingenuous if he now claims that he doesn't have the B/C/S version, that between the 15th of May last year and whilst this witness was on the stand he didn't point out to us that whilst he has the English version, the B/C/S version did not accompany it. We'll check again. If it didn't precede that, we'll certainly supply him with a copy, but he has that English version and never brought it to our attention until yesterday -- in fact, until today, because yesterday he is still quoting that ERN number, that document which he does have. We -- a check was done on the -- well, after the pre-trial brief was filed to double-check disclosure. We thought it was all complied with on the 15th of May. It is continuously ongoing. Any time a document does come up, a witness brings in a document, it is disclosed to Defence. I don't think the Defence -- in fact, I think Mr. Pantelic, although he has not invoked a Rule 66(B) and is not in a situation of reciprocal discovery, we have treated him like we have treated any other defendant -- any other Defence members, and I find it somewhat disingenuous that he is calling into question our good faith in the process. As I say, if -- so we are -- we've also put in -- since yesterday, we realised that there was an oversight. We have rechecked all our witnesses, which is why the statement of Mr. Dagovic came to our attention. And we've also put in a system whereby in the weeks before the next witness comes, we'll be rechecking individually every single witness with our files and with the receipts and that to make it -- it will be the fourth or fifth time this is gone through but to make sure there cannot, I hope, ever, you know, be this oversight that would in some way interrupt these proceedings before the Chamber. So if there's anything else on our behalf that the Chamber would like us to do, then of course we'd be happy to undertake that if they are of the opinion that there has been a problem with the disclosure process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will deal with the matters discussed by counsel at a later stage. In the meantime, we'll proceed with the cross-examination of the witness. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir, again. We're into the third day of our questioning. I would like to assure you that we don't have many more questions as far as Mr. Zaric's defence is concerned, and we're hoping to cover what questions we do have pretty quickly. Yesterday we stopped at the event relating to the dismantling of the radiators and the central heating equipment which you described here in your statement. We noted, in agreement with our learned friends from the Prosecution, that you did not mention that event in your statement given to The Hague Tribunal investigators on the 14th and 17th of June, 1996. The way things look now and after everything that happened, it seems that the first time you mentioned this event was in July 1998, some, let's say, five years after the event; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you several questions on that topic. You said that you know Simo Zaric. The Prosecutor asked you about this already. I would now like to go back to the time period before the outbreak of the conflict. Can you tell me where Simo Zaric lived at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Mose Pijade settlement. It was called 64 Apartments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are buildings with several apartments; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. The witness, I saw that he was speaking at the same time as me. It was really not my mistake, but I will instruct the witness to speak slow and to wait until I finish with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have fallen into the same trap again of speaking at the same time, I would just ask you kindly to wait until I have finished my question. If my information is correct, these are buildings with central heating, and perhaps you were even working when -- when you were working in the public utility, you were working on the installation of the new central heating and the water system.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the Prosecutors, or to be precise, to the investigators of the Prosecutor's Office, it states that you took this to the house of Simo Zaric; is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there's a mistake there, but I know where we unloaded these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you did not take this to Simo Zaric's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric did not have a house in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you tell this to the investigators or did you tell them that this was taken to Simo Zaric's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible that there was a mistake there. But I do know that this was unloaded before the house of Fadil Topcagic, Simo's wife's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already stated that before the Trial Chamber. But I just have one more question concerning Odzak. In the second half of August and the beginning of September, so up until the 7th, when you said that you were arrested, so did you go to Odzak in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Simo Zaric in Odzak in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So now we are speaking, in order to clear things up, we are speaking about the second half of August and early September, so before the 7th of September, because after that you didn't go to Odzak. So in that period, did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the end of your examination-in-chief, the Prosecutor took you back to the event in front of the AS Cafe and he asked you several questions so I would like to clarify a few matters on that topic. He asked you about a certain Nebojsa Stankovic called Cera, and you said that he was a member of the 4th Detachment; is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was in uniform and that he was sitting in front of the cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know whether he was a member of the 4th Detachment or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After that, did you used to see this Cera in Samac during the period while you were still free, so in the period before you were arrested in September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him a couple of times, but I avoided him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course. It's a natural reaction. And then when you were arrested, did you used to see him at the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you one more thing about Cera. Was he, when you saw him -- when you said that you saw him and avoided him, was he often in the company of these specials, these people in camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With Your Honour's permission, I have almost finished with my cross-examination. Now I would like the witness to see again the tape that was already played at the beginning of his examination-in-chief. This is the tape entitled "Genocide in Bosanski Samac." It is already tendered into evidence under number P16, and the transcript of this tape is recorded as P60A in the evidence. I don't believe that we are going to need the transcript or use it. We will see just one very, very small portion. It lasts maybe ten, maybe 15 seconds, and if you permit, I would like to show this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You gave it to the technical booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I already gave it to the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You can stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, at the beginning of your testimony, the Prosecutor showed you a tape; is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And what you have just seen now, that's the tape; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At that point, the Prosecutor asked for the tape to be stopped and he asked you, "Do you recognise this voice;" is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you do recognise it and that this is the -- that is the voice of Simo Zaric; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me now, what you see on the screen, who is this person sitting on the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that man on TV for the first time when the Samac mosque was shown, the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, on the left side of the screen, not on the right side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is the TV editor of TV Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And who is this other person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in uniform?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So it's Simo Zaric. And can you please tell me what it says here on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Simo Zaric, deputy commander," and I don't see any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So at the time when the Prosecutor asked you to -- if you recognised the voice in front of you on the screen, you could see the picture of Simo Zaric, under that you could see the name "Simo Zaric," and the title, "assistant commander;" is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. The next counsel? Yes, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir, my name is Slobodan Zecevic. I will be asking you certain questions. Sir, could you please tell me, is your whole family from Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You have five brothers; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did have five brothers, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And one of your brothers has deceased?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Throughout the war, and after the war, your brothers continued to live in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if your questioning is likely to bring out the family names, maybe we better go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't want him to mention the name of the brothers, just the brothers in general but the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It was likely to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm so sorry. I don't need the private session at this moment because I'm practically finished with this line of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So the names will be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So one of your brothers in any case has remained and lives in Samac after the end of the war. Please don't speak his name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, can you please tell me, you served in the army, in the former Yugoslavia; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, you were a military conscript; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my age, I was supposed to be, and I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have a military ID card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also had a reserve wartime assignment, which was in your military ID booklet; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, could you please tell us where you were assigned, where your wartime assignment was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first assignment was in the reserve police as a career. Then I was transferred to a company, to the civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In April 1992, what was your wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left the company at that time, and I was on the records of the civilian protection at the water works.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So that means that at the time of immediate danger of war, you were obliged to report to your place of mobilisation at the waterworks; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't report to your wartime assignment; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the former Yugoslavia, besides the military duties or service, there was also work duty? You knew that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that there was work duty in the former Yugoslavia, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify something. In case of immediate threat of war and war, there was military service, that duty, and also general work duty; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just stated that I had never heard of work duty. If I was summoned, of course I would have to report in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you served in the army and you are familiar with the regulations, do you know that it was your duty that at the moment that war was declared or immediate threat of war was declared you were obliged to report to your place of mobilisation at the waterworks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, if the question's being divided into two parts, I wouldn't have an objection. I don't know -- first of all, I don't know if the answer "yes" means that the witness is saying he's familiar with the wartime regulations or whether his answer relates to the latter part he knew that he was obliged to report. So that's uncertain. But there's thus far nothing to show that he had any familiarity with any of the wartime regulations. Whether he's qualified to speak about those wartime regulations is utterly uncertain. If my friend wants to ask him questions about that and find out what his qualifications are, that might be another matter, but that hasn't occurred thus far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But isn't that a matter you can clear in your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, it is, but whilst --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I suppose it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- if you want me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You clear that. Anything that's not clear, unless it's an obvious mistake, then you wait for your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have asked the witness concerning his knowledge because he was a member -- he served a military service in the former Yugoslavia and of course he knows what is his duty as an army reserve, of course. And he confirmed that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you know, I'm asking you do you know that you were subject to the regulations, legal penalties if you did not respond to the mobilisation call in case of immediate danger of war or of war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object at this time to the question. Your Honour, this was raised with a previous witness concerning the regulations of the former Yugoslavia. In this case, we are arguing that there were new countries which existed in the spring of 1992, and this question was raised previously whether these regulations would apply, and we previously objected when one of the unnamed witnesses was testifying in late November and December, and this Court did sustain and agree that those regulations or at least that question was not a fair question as to whether or not they were still required to report that those regulations or the laws did in fact still apply, because the former Yugoslavia did not exist in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, I have asked the witness on his personal knowledge. I'm not asking for a legal opinion or anything like that, just his personal knowledge. At the same time, I understand the point which my learned colleague is raising, but, Your Honours, the obligation and the thing -- whether this -- the former Yugoslavia ceased to exist or not is a matter which is up for this Trial Chamber to decide, and at this point, we know that the regulations at that time were applicable, that the regulation of the former Yugoslavia and the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were applicable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But that is your -- yeah. That is your assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is my assertion, as well as the assertion of the Prosecutor that these same regulations did not apply. So what I am asking, I'm just asking from the witness a personal opinion, whether he knows that he is committing a criminal offence by not responding to the mobilisation or going to the mobilisation point at the time of war danger or wartime. That is the only thing I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It cannot be a criminal offence, Your Honour, because the nation did not exist. The republic -- even the Republika Srpska or Yugoslavia did not exist as it did when those regulations were written or when those regulations were drafted and adopted. Therefore, it can't be a violation. At the least, Your Honour, it is a legal issue that this gentleman, who has training as a plumber, should not be answering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Yeah. Mr. Zecevic, you understood what the Prosecution is saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That is a submission you can make.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah. But you can't ask for the witness's opinion even.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking, Your Honours, his personal opinion, because the basis of his obligation is his service at the military -- at the army of the former Yugoslavia. So that is where his obligation derivates from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But that is the -- that is in issue. So the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the other thing is: What regulations are these? Have they been identified?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Sorry. What regulations are these? Have they been identified? Do we have the name of the regulation? Do we have the particular clause? We don't quite know what this is at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, first of all, during the cross-examination of Mr. Tihic, we have presented some legal documents concerning the military obligation, but this was subject to the objection from the Prosecution that these military laws applied to Republika Srpska and therefore cannot be -- their assertion is that this is not for the overall Bosnia and Herzegovina. What we are planning to do is that in the Defence case we present all the relevant data, all the relevant laws which in our opinion were applicable at that time, because immediately after the -- after the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: No. If you wanted to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: If you want him to answer the question, perhaps you want to identify whatever you have there that regulates his work duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Of course eventually that's a question of law, as the Court has just ruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a question of law beyond any dispute. What I was asking is a personal opinion of knowledge of this witness, because he had a military ID in which it is clearly stated, and he can confirm - I can ask him if you allow me to - it says that the person is committing a criminal offence if he doesn't, in a time of near war danger or war, go to his mobilisation point. That is what I'm asking the witness. And he should know that because everybody had his own military book or military ID in the reserve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you may ask the witness that if you're talking about the contents of his ID, military book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you did have your military ID booklet with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That booklet has some 20 pages or so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It also lists the provisions of the law on the armed forces valid at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Among them is the provision according to which a person who fails to respond to the call-up is subject to criminal responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That booklet was valid until March 1992 when a referendum was held in Bosnia and Herzegovina, after which it was proclaimed to be an independent state. I believe it was valid up until that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would really like you to answer only my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... there is a confusion here. If maybe -- yeah. If I'm right, what you are asking the witness to say, to confirm, is what is contained in that ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is there that writing that if you don't attend to your call-up you will be committing a criminal offence, just to state that. It's not whether or not it was applicable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's right. That's exactly what I wanted to say to the witness, to refrain to my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- to answer my question only and not to go into the specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We don't know if it was applicable, yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please answer my question. Was this contained in the booklet regardless of the validity of the booklet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you did read that. So you were familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A long time ago but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Despite all that, you did not go to the mobilisation location because you believed that after March, it was no longer valid.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, I considered it not to be valid, but I did not go.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone inform you officially that it was no longer valid or did you decide on your own that it was no longer valid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I decided that for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just make a pause, before answering, for interpretation. Thank you. Can we agree that by failing to respond to the mobilisation call-up you, in effect, indicated that you did not want to take part in the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not want to join any army, that army or any other army. And also I was unable to leave my house because there was shooting going on and I didn't want to be involved in the war in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell me whether this decision of yours, and this idea that you had that this booklet did not bind you any more, have anything to do with your -- with the fact that you were of a certain ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I considered this military ID booklet to be a booklet of another state, that belonged to another state.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now have a look at a document that the Prosecution has already shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May the usher please show the document D22E/2 ter, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, do you mean P22?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: "D", "D" like doughnut.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since this document is under seal, maybe we should go into a closed session. I'm sorry, I missed that it was under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. So we will go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will now talk some more about the work duty, along the same lines that you discussed this topic with the Prosecutor. Just a moment, please. During the examination by the Prosecutor, on the 4th of December, 2001, at page 50 -- 5111, when the Prosecutor asked you the following question, which I will now read in English and then I will read out your answer, too, and you will get the interpretation: [In English] "In all of the time that you were engaged in this sort of labour, this sort of project, did anyone ever record, write down, in any way at all, the days that you worked or the hours that you worked?" "No." Answer: "No." [Interpretation] Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I still have the same answer: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, please tell me, on the 3rd of December, during the examination-in-chief conducted by the Prosecution, on page 5041, line 5 through 8 -- 4 through 8, sorry, when the Prosecutor asked you how you knew what it was all about when you first went to do your work duty and about all the things that happened when you reported for the first time, you stated -- I will now again read it out in English and it will be interpreted to you: [In English] "When we arrived, the lists were read out to us. In fact they called out our names, to see if everyone has responded to the call-up. Since most people had, they went upstairs into the building. I think it was Dzemal Kapetanovic, and the other one was Bozo Ninkovic. After a while, we were divided into those labour groups. We didn't know where we were going or what we were required to do."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this what you stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So somebody must have called out your names from a list of some kind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When they called out your names, that was the way in which they ascertained who responded to the call-up and who didn't; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And after that, they assigned you to various work groups and sent you to carry out some tasks in various locations in Samac and its environs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that there was some kind of a record kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, the records existed only to show who showed up and who doesn't. The person who failed to show up was arrested by the police. That was the only reason why it existed, as a sort of control mechanism.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, I read out to you what you stated on the 4th of December, and that is when you said that there was -- there were no records. You confirmed to the Prosecutor that there were no records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, they would read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, the witness said in examination-in-chief that there were no records of work done, work performed, hours worked. That's what there was no record of, and that was the thrust of his evidence. Now it's being put to him that somehow he's contradicting his position because he agrees that there must have been a list or something for people to answer in the first place to the call-up. But they're completely different records, and they address different issues. They're recording different things, and from that point of view, the question is misleading to the witness, I submit. One --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One deals with call-up and one deals with record of work done, and they're the two differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see that it's the time. Shall I pose that -- shall I answer this question or pose another question? Because I see it's a quarter to 4.00 already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. di Fazio's point has been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I will read again the transcript, because the transcript says -- the question of Mr. di Fazio was:

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In all of the time that you were engaged in this sort of labour, these sort of projects, did anyone ever record or write down in any way at all the days that you worked or the hours that you worked? And he said "No." But it's obvious when he shows for call-up somebody would put a cross on his name that he showed for work that day. Isn't that right? I mean, it sounds logical to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But, Mr. Zecevic, that's a different question. I mean, your name can be called out --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: -- you can come on a particular day --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: -- and what the official does, what he records, I mean, is he privy to that? I mean, for that matter, if you had asked him a question, which probably would have been more proper, "You did go for -- you did report for duty on particular days, and you did go at a particular time and come back at a different time. From there, records could have been made of the number of hours you worked." That would be quite another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Shall I pose that question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Let's go for our break and you will ponder the issues raised, and we will continue at 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic? You're proceeding with cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, before the break, you confirmed that you were called out in the morning, there was a roll-call in the morning when you reported for work duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are not aware of anyone keeping any records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May the usher please show the witness P39 ter, "P" like Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, it's just a -- I wonder if the Chamber would indulge the Prosecution for a moment. We seem to have lost our copy of P39. Might I just have a look at the court exhibit, please, just to see if I can refresh my memory as to what it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can just -- you can approach the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I wonder if it's ID -- an ID document, or is it a full exhibit at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's your document. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we confirm from the registry, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it's an ID document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Before we go on to this document, I have just one question for you. When you were called out for work duty, somebody came out and read out the names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that anything was written down or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the names were read out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And those who did not -- who were not there to respond, a mark was made next to their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the person reading out the names, if somebody had failed to show up, that person made a mark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know what kind of notes he made, of course?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at this document. The Prosecutor showed you this document, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please read out the title?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, "Clerks and others for the work brigade tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you answered the questions put to you by the Prosecutor, you said that persons under numbers 1 and 2, whose jobs are indicated as clerks, that they became clerks only in mid-July, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You also said that the persons who used to be clerks swam over the River Sava; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The two persons here under numbers 1 and 2 --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please wait for me to finish my question. The two persons listed here under numbers 1 and 2 are Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The previous clerks were also Muslims; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, all the names listed here as 1 through 9, are they all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You confirmed that the first two persons listed under 1 and 2, before they became clerks that they were involved in the work duty.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You started with your work duty on the 17th of May, 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that before that date you do not have any personal knowledge as to who was involved in the work duty and who wasn't?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I don't need that document any more. Could you please show the document D23/2 ter. I'm not sure whether it's ID or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please have a look at this list and tell me whether this list refers to the same nine persons that were listed on the previous exhibit that you had examined a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the exception of Miladeta Bajraktarevic. She was not there. I think that's the only change. So Miladeta Bajraktarevic was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, the persons listed as 1 and 2 are the same persons who were listed on the previous document also under 1 and 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Above their name -- names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I have to interrupt you. For the sake of the record being clearer, can we have the other document you're referring to given to the witness so that when you ask -- you say the list on D23 is the same as D22, or whatever, so he has both.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, Your Honour. I'm sorry for this. Yes, please. If the usher can show the other document as well, the previous document. It's P39 ter. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So when you ask the question, you actually give us the ID number of the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no difference. The two documents are the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please -- [Interpretation] Could you please put both documents on the ELMO, one next to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please have another look and check whether the same persons are listed on documents P39 ter and D23/2 ter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same persons. The same persons are listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please now look at this document which is now on the ELMO, that's document D23/2 ter? Could you please read what's written in the lower right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Certified by Sejfudin Sejdinovic".

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, Sejfudin Sejdinovic is the clerk who is listed under number 1 on this same document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, when you went to do your work duty, who called you, in fact, if you remember? Was it somebody -- was it one of the two clerks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: A courier came and brought me a list that I was supposed to sign, and he told me that I was to report the next day. The names were there but there was no signature by Sejfudin. I think that Bozo Ninkovic and Dzemal Kapetanovic were at that time and Sabahudin Nogic [Real-time transcript read in error "had much"].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this document, D23/2 ter, there are headings with the months listed here. You have April, May, June, July, August, total number of days, total amount, and remarks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Below each of the headings for the month, there is a certain number listed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I wonder whether we could get a clarification of what we've got here in the transcript? Page 42, lines 22 and 23 doesn't make too much sense, as you can see. It says, "I think that Bozo Ninkovic and Dzemal Kapetanovic were at that time and Sabahudin Nogic had much."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, by all means. I wasn't following the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you who it was that called you to go to the work duty the first time, whether it was one of the clerks, you said that a courier came, brought me a list, I was supposed to sign it and then you said -- you mentioned Sabahudin Nogic, Dzemal Kapetanovic and another person. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were clerks. Bozo was the chief clerk and Sabahudin Nogic and this other person, Dzemal Kapetanovic, was also there. Dzemal Rogic [as interpreted] was digging trenches with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please go about this slowly. So on the 17th of May, 1992, when you went to do your work duty for the first time, the clerks were Dzemal Kapetanovic and Bozo Ninkovic. Bozo Ninkovic was the chief clerk and Dzemal Kapetanovic and Sabahudin Nogic were clerks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So these two gentlemen, Dzemal Kapetanovic and Sabahudin Nogic, are the two clerks you were speaking about when you said that they swam over the River Sava?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and that's when the other two persons became clerks. That was in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the two gentlemen listed in document D23/2 ter, Sejfudin Sejdinovic and this other gentleman, they became clerks in July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We started discussing the figures below the headings for months, and the total number of days. In your opinion, do these figures represent the number of days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the number of days that a person --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honour please, it's very difficult for this witness, who can only speculate as to what those figures might represent. We ran into this difficulty, I think, with the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, it's something that my learned friend --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He's not the maker of the documents so --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No. Not only that. There is nothing to indicate he's an expert accountant or familiar with this sort of material. It's something that Mr. Zecevic might be able to submit to you, of course, but whether this witness can say anything about it is another matter altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will withdraw that question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one last question, please. In the lower right-hand corner, it says, "Certified by Sejfudin Sejdinovic;" is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that by his signature, he certifies the accuracy of the information contained here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Again, that is a question that can't be answered by the witness, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will withdraw that question as well. Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Mr. Usher, I don't have any more questions on that document.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please tell me, you worked at the waterworks in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Safet Hadzialijagic nicknamed Coner also worked at the waterworks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was he a manager of the waterworks or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the manager of the plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, he was your superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During your testimony while my colleague Mr. Lukic was questioning you regarding that statement at the police station, you said that the part that pertains to your relationship with Mr. Hadzialijagic is true; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You had a dispute with him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the dispute was about or you perhaps don't wish to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a dispute when we were both -- it was a conflict when we were still in the Communist Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you and Mr. Hadzialijagic were members of the League of Communists of Yugoslavia. This was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I am to assist Mr. Zecevic. I am not objecting at this stage, because I assume that this is an issue going to credit. It's being developed to attack the credit of this witness. And if that's the case, then it may be relevant. If it's not, then it's difficult to see what possible relevance his disputes with other people in Bosanski Samac have to the proceedings. So I'm not objecting, but because I've made that assumption I hope my assumption is correct, because if I am incorrect, then I most certainly am objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It may be relevant -- it may be only necessary to say -- for the witness to state whether or not there was a dispute without going into the details of the dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't want to go into the details. I asked the witness whether he can tell us that or not. If he had said no, then that would be enough. It goes into -- it goes into the matter of the credibility of the witness, and as well, I am building the foundation, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- for my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are the details of the dispute relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, they are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Then we don't get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We're not getting them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said that both of you were members of the League of Communists before the -- before April 1992. How long were you a member of the League of Communists? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a long time ago. I think that I became a member in 1998 or -- I'm sorry, in 1988 or 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that when you became a member or when you stopped being a member of the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when I stopped being a member of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And after that, and also Mr. Hadzialijagic, as far as you know, we both moved to the SDA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time I did not join the SDA because it didn't exist at the time I left the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When did you become a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when Mr. Hadzialijagic became a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three months after I joined the SDA. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And after that he became a member of the executive board of the Samac SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, because I left the SDA at the time that he joined the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So his joining of the party was the reason why you yourself left the party; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that we've touched upon this topic, could you please tell me, sir, the judgement of the military court, as we've already heard, declared you -- found you guilty and sentenced you to a prison sentence for, amongst other things, wounding Mr. Stevan Arandjic on the 17th of April, 1992; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You claimed here that these facts are not true. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see, sir, Stevan Arandjic on the 17th of April or in that period in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen days before the war -- this is Fadil Mustafic's neighbour, so I would see him when I would go to visit his son Dino. That's when I would see Stevan, because they live next door to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see him after the 16th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see him at all or you didn't see him in that period in April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall. Perhaps in passing, but I generally did not see him, because when I started to perform the work duty, we would leave at 7.00 in the morning. We would be taken there, and we would be brought back in the evening. So I didn't have any time to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You started your work duty on the 19th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Stevan Arandjic between the 16th of April and the 17th of May? Did you see him at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you already know that I was beaten up at that time and that both of my arms were hurt. My collarbones were broken, so I couldn't move. I couldn't walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know that. I'm just asking you simply if you had seen him or not.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you explained to us that after your exchange, you gave a statement to the police, I think in Orasje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first statement I gave was in Tuzla, because I came from the other side. So you had to go to the police. The police was -- were waiting for us, and they were taking our statements. So I had to give a statement upon my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 27th of July, 1994, you gave a statement to the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If you perhaps mean the one in Domaljevac to Sead Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, to Sead Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this -- do you agree that this was on the 27th of July, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but I know it was in 1994. It was summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You gave this statement at the police station in Domaljevac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this Sead Mujkanovic, he was a police officer and you gave your statement to him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time he was a police official, but, yes, he was a police officer in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this Mujkanovic from earlier, from Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when you gave your statement to him, did you -- were you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one thing that I was silent about. I did not dare mention my brothers. He would always ask me where they were, if I had any contacts with my brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So everything else contained in the statement is true; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. But I would like to see it. Maybe you can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to your recollection, was there any reason for you to lie to Sead Mujkanovic once you were released from Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned this one thing. The first thing that Sead asked me was about my brothers. I don't know any other reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I don't think that's the way to challenge a witness, like he indicated that maybe he should see the statement. I'm sure you can't expect him to remember every word since 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. By all means, Your Honours. I understand. And I just have one more question and I will show him the statement, and then he can verify whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: About the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Not the contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me, do you remember if you signed this statement at the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can the usher please -- I would like to introduce into evidence the statement given by this witness. Just one second. This is a statement given on the 27th July 1994, number is 03-12/5-02-31/94. The statement was given at the Ministry of Interior, Police Headquarters Derventa, Police Station Bosanski Samac. This document was disclosed to us by the Prosecutor. We have it in Serbo-Croat and in English, and we have copies for -- here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, what is the purpose of wanting to put this in?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: What is the purpose of wanting to put in the whole statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because I would like to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: The specific purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, there -- there are at least three specific questions. Two of them deal with the contents of the statement and his previous testimony, and one -- one deals with the -- with the -- no, no, no. I'm sorry. It deals with the -- with the formal sign of the statement -- the signature on this statement, because as you will see, the signature on this statement is almost identical to the signature in the -- on the previous statement which was denied by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you're not telling the Trial Chamber that you're trying to challenge the witness on the signature in this manner?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just trying to challenge the witness on the contents of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yeah. I hope not the signature, because we are not going to do it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the position of the Prosecution? Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Well, the ultimate purpose of what Mr. Zecevic is trying to do, I assume, is to establish prior inconsistent statements. If that's his object, then that's a perfectly proper object -- objective, I should say. The manner in which it's to be accomplished is another issue. Whether it necessitates putting in the statement into evidence, I don't think is necessary. Surely, the witness can be shown the passages, perhaps read out the passages, refresh his memory, and then Mr. Zecevic can ask him: "Look, that's what it says" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. Mr. di Fazio, Mr. Zecevic has stated what he wants to do. Is the Prosecution objecting? This question of going behind the submission and suggesting what the intentions are will not be allowed at this stage. I think it's better for you. You know these documents came from your office. If you have any objection, you state your reasons. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, with respect, it's difficult for me to say whether I object or not because I don't know the purpose for which it's being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But that is a matter for submission. You can make submissions after that, when you notice that it's being used in ways which you didn't expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. If that is the case, then I would have no objection to its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You wanted to say something else? Yes, you can make a submission.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, is the name of an individual who was raped in here? Could this be held at least privately or under seal so it just won't be public?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Can we have the numbers, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D26/2 ter for the B/C/S and D26/2 for the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Zecevic, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, have you looked at this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 2? There are two signatures. One is a signature of Sead Mujkanovic and the other is yours; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your statement that you gave to Sead Mujkanovic on the 27th of July, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that Sejo maybe put in some -- augmented it a little bit. That was his job. But yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the things that you stated are generally contained in this statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly read the third paragraph, and it begins with --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the beginning of the war."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's the third passage from the top of the page, from the top of the statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I meant the third paragraph, the one that starts, "At the onset of the war."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, this document is under seal but then the particulars have been read out, so that has to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. I'm sorry. I said the third paragraph and the witness started reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is a problem because we've always said if you want a paragraph read, please, can counsel read it out? And then the witness will obviously follow and then the translators will do their job and then you can ask your questions later. Then we avoid this sort of problems and even the delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would be more than glad to read the paragraph, if I may now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I will read and you can follow it in your statement, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you read slowly, slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: "At the onset of the war, when the town came under Serbo-Chetnik attack, I was at home. That day, I saw the following persons armed and in uniform in their army. And those people -- the following persons: Djordje Pisarevic, known as Ruka, probably, son of Andrija, born in 1945; Stevan Arandzic, in brackets, Stevo Milic's son-in-law; Aco Vasic, Milan Celikovic, in brackets, the manager of the cooperative farm. Jovo Ikanovic, from Dugo Polje." And so on and so forth. Is this true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names have been changed a little bit so I don't know whether it's true that I saw Stevan. That's what it says here but I'm not sure that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you claim that you did not see him but still it states so here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this statement read to you before you signed it, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was read to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you signed it without any remarks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will read another passage. This is the last sentence on the first page: "On the 8th of August" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify the English version, Your Honour, if I could assist you. It's -- in the English version, it's the -- yes, it's the second paragraph, the first sentence on the second page. It's -- in the English version, that's the -- that is the sentence I'm going to read. [Interpretation] "On the 8th of September, 1992, after I returned from working in Odzak, in front of the retirement home in Bosanski Samac, Stevan Arandzic saw me there and I was immediately on that day taken to the detention room in the SUP building." Do you remember having stated that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, though, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: The day when I was arrested, I did not go to work. I think that in my testimony, and in my statements, I did -- in my previous statements, I said that I was ill, I couldn't go to work, and the police came and picked me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So it is not correct that Stevan Arandzic saw you in front of the retirement home and that you were arrested immediately after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
